description: Pipeline YAML fail-fast conformance (issue #33 §1.2): a `pipeline:` section that names a step which does not exist in the active strategy MUST raise at parse time, not warn and continue. `configure` is an OBJECT MAP keyed by step name — that is what schemas/apcore-config.schema.json $defs/PipelineConfig declares and what all three SDKs parse (apcore-python pipeline_config.py:187, apcore-typescript pipeline-config.ts:244, apcore-rust pipeline_config.rs:320). An earlier revision of this fixture used an array of {name, ...} objects, which no SDK accepts.

test_cases.description: YAML configures a step name that does not exist in the active strategy; ConfigurationError MUST be raised at parse time

expected.error_class_name_is_not_the_contract: All three SDKs name the class/variant ConfigurationError; only error_code is normative.

test_cases.description: A step declares requires: ['validated_inputs'] but no upstream step provides it; PipelineDependencyError MUST be raised at strategy construction (before first call())

expected.error_class_name_is_not_the_contract: All three SDKs name the class PipelineDependencyError; only error_code is normative.

test_cases.description: When all requires: are satisfied by upstream provides:, strategy construction MUST succeed without warnings

driver_contract.assert_the_wire_code: Assert `expected.error_code`, the cross-language wire string. The previous revision asserted `error_type: "ConfigurationError"` — a CLASS name that all three SDKs coincidentally share — and so reported green while the three emitted three DIFFERENT wire codes: Python PIPELINE_CONFIGURATION_ERROR, TypeScript PIPELINE_CONFIG_INVALID, Rust CONFIGURATION_ERROR. A fixture that asserts the one attribute that happens to agree proves nothing.
driver_contract.canonical_code: PIPELINE_CONFIGURATION_ERROR, per docs/spec/2026-05-decision-log.md and the registry in features/error-system.md. PIPELINE_CONFIG_INVALID is a DIFFERENT code in that registry — field-level validation failure — and MUST NOT be reused for unknown-step references.
driver_contract.parse_time: The raise MUST happen while the config is being turned into a strategy, not on first call. A driver that only asserts 'it raised eventually' cannot tell the two apart: build the strategy and assert it raises there, without executing anything.
driver_contract.the_valid_key_must_really_exist: `input_validation` is a REAL built-in step (apcore-python builtin_steps.py, apcore-typescript builtin-steps.ts:593, apcore-rust builtin_steps.rs:124). An earlier revision used `validate_input`, which exists in no SDK — so the case would have raised on the FIRST key and the `error_message_contains: nonexistent_step` assertion could never be reached. The valid half of a fail-fast test has to actually be valid.
driver_contract.one_way_to_say_it: Every case expresses its expected failure as `error_code`. There is no `error_type` key: a class name is a per-language detail that can agree while the wire codes diverge, which is exactly how the configure case hid a three-way split.
